risk_if_not_implemented: Without Data Mining Protection, sensitive and/or regulated data may be disclosed, altered or lost through inadequate classification, handling or protection. Based on the risk and threat mapping for this control, this deficiency most likely exposes the organization to Loss of Confidentiality (R-IP-2), and most likely increases susceptibility to Malicious Cyber Activity (MT-2).

compensating_control_1.name: Access Enforcement
compensating_control_1.description: Mechanisms exist to enforce Logical Access Control (LAC) permissions that conform to the principle of "least privilege."
compensating_control_1.justification: Access Enforcement (IAC-25) provides access control enforcement that compensates for the absence of Data Mining Protection (DCH-24.1) by restricting system and data access to authorized users through alternative identity and access mechanisms. Given the data-handling focus of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.

compensating_control_2.name: Data Loss Prevention (DLP)
compensating_control_2.description: Automated mechanisms exist to implement Data Loss Prevention (DLP) to protect sensitive information as it is stored, transmitted and processed.
compensating_control_2.justification: Data Loss Prevention (DLP) (DCH-40) provides detective monitoring capability that compensates for the absence of Data Mining Protection (DCH-24.1) by identifying unauthorized, anomalous, or non-compliant activity that the primary control would have prevented. Given the data-handling focus of this control, this compensating control targets the same underlying risk objective through an alternative approach, helping to maintain an acceptable level of residual risk until the primary control can be implemented.
